correctness.rationale: The source theoretical LINEX Bayes action contains a negative exponent, so replacing the posterior expectation by an empirical posterior average must preserve that sign. The later printed positive exponent makes the estimator strictly negative whenever the asymmetry parameter and target draws are positive. For the source simulation truth 1.3, any such estimate has squared error greater than 1.69, contradicting the reported LINEX MSE 0.0032. The packaged checker independently verifies these sign and error bounds on positive draw sequences.

value.rationale: The paper treats LINEX as one of four principal Bayesian loss functions and compares their finite-sample performance. Eq. (4.11) is presented as the executable MCMC approximation used to turn posterior draws into the LINEX estimate, yet its literal output has the wrong sign for the paper’s positive targets under the main asymmetry setting. Correcting the exponent is therefore necessary for reproducibility of a central Bayesian component and explains why the published tables cannot come from the printed formula.
